newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares surge again as market squeezed up.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares surge again as market squeezed up.

text.p: Belgian shares surged again on Monday, closing at record levels, as the market continued to be squeezed higher by professional investors, dealers said.
The blue chip Bel-20 index added 31.28 points, or 1.26 percent, to 2,504.37 points, defying analysts warnings last week of a correction if the 2,500 level was breached.

One trader said the move was artificially inflated because of the difficulty in finding paper to make complete "baskets" of Bel-20 components -- the basis of most derivative trades on the index. He felt sure the record run would eventually end in tears, but when was difficult to predict.
"You need 160 UCB shares to make a basket. You can get 80 or so no problem but have to really pay for the rest...and UCB counts for five index points," he said, citing one example.
Chemicals and drugs maker UCB ended the day 2,400 francs higher at 124,300.
A sharp rise in retailer Colruyt, which gained 900 francs, or 4.75 percent, to 19,850 francs was a similar story, he said.

"It can continue like this if buyers are still there, but as soon as they stop the downside is going to be very painful," he said. If no correction came earlier, he expected disappointment over first-half 1997 results due in September to trigger losses.
Dealers said, however, banks at the moment remained committed to covering the launch of new and revamped index-linked investment funds.
Both Kredietbank and Generale Bank are at present promoting such funds.
Monday's basket buying helped to lift most prices, with Generale Bank and Kredietbank the only blue chips to end unchanged. Rival bank Dexia CC also lagged, ending down 10 francs at 3,800.
However, insurer Fortis AG added 2.69 percent at 8,010 francs. One trader said AG was now leading its Dutch sister company Fortis AMEV higher, whereas normally it was the other way round.
